records.name: Tabernacle United Church
records.summary: A progressive congregation on Chestnut Street that worships in person and on Zoom and holds a community meal on the third Saturday of each month.
records.what_you_do: Come to Sunday worship at 10 am in person or on Zoom, or join the community meal on the third Saturday from 1 to 3 pm.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 10 am in person and on Zoom. Community meal on the third Saturday of each month, 1 to 3 pm.

cost.text: The site does not state a cost for worship or the community meal.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 10 am at 3700 Chestnut Street, or ask the office at 215-386-4100 for Zoom details.
first_step.basis: The site says all people are welcome and gives worship times and an office contact, but it describes no newcomer program or membership path.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday worship starts at 10 am, held in person at the church or on Zoom. The October 4, 2026 service included Holy Communion. Masks are optional for in-person worship, and the site does not say how long a service runs. The community meal is in person only, on the third Saturday from 1 to 3 pm.
first_visit_tips: Call the office at 215-386-4100 on a Tuesday or Thursday, 10 am to 3 pm, for Zoom details or questions about access.
Masks are optional for in-person worship, so wear one if you like.
The site does not list parking, transit or step-free entry, so ask the office before you come.

records.notes: The homepage mentions a newcomer welcome video, but no link to it was found on the homepage or the About page, so it is not cited. Newcomer rating lowered from 4 (tier 1) to 3 because no newcomer program or video page could be confirmed. Office hours are Tuesday and Thursday, 10 am to 3 pm, or by appointment. Status and sign of life updated from the October 4, 2026 service post.

records.name: Tabor Lutheran Church
records.summary: A Lutheran congregation in North Philadelphia with Sunday worship at 10:30 am, in person and online. The church runs Katie's Cupboard, a food pantry at its building that is open Thursday mornings.
records.what_you_do: Visit Katie's Cupboard on a Thursday morning for food, or attend Sunday worship at 10:30 am in person or watch the virtual service.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 10:30 am in person, with a virtual service usually posted by 6 pm on Sundays. Communion on the first and third Sundays. Katie's Cupboard food pantry is open Thursdays, 10 am to noon.

locations.label: Katie's Cupboard food pantry (back door of the church)

access.notes: The church says the sanctuary is not wheelchair accessible. The site does not say whether the pantry entrance is step-free.

first_step.how: Go to Katie's Cupboard on a Thursday between 10 am and noon, using the back door of the church at 4860 N Howard Street.
first_step.basis: The pantry is open to anyone facing food insecurity on set Thursday hours, and the church invites visitors to Sunday worship. The site lists no newcomer program.
first_step.what_to_expect: The pantry is open Thursdays from 10 am to noon at the back door of the church. Most of its food comes from SHARE, and you fill in a registration form for that food. Masks are required in the pantry, and bringing your own bags helps because the pantry hands out bags to people.
first_visit_tips: Wear a mask, which the pantry asks everyone to do.
Bring your own bags to take food home, if you have them.
Call the church office at 215-455-1706 before you come if you need step-free entry, since the site says the sanctuary is not wheelchair accessible.
Ask the office what food is available to people who do not register, since the pantry says some food can still be given out.

records.notes: Pantry hours (Thursdays 10 am to noon) came from the pantry's own page and were not on the tier 1 pages. The homepage states the sanctuary is not wheelchair accessible. The virtual service is usually posted by 6 pm on Sundays. The newsletter sign up form on the site shows a setup message. No dated last sign of life is cited: the virtual worship video is labeled for the week of October 4, but the year appears only in an image path.

records.name: Friends of Tacony Creek Park
records.summary: Neighbors and visitors who look after Tacony Creek Park, a 300-acre watershed park in lower Northeast Philadelphia. The group runs free group walks and runs on the trails.
records.what_you_do: Join a free group walk or run on the trails, or volunteer for park cleanups, planting days and storm drain marking through the online form.

schedule.text: Weekly group walks and runs, called Walk with Me and Run with Me, plus other trail programs. The Friends site points to a partner events calendar for days and times.

access.notes: A 3.2-mile paved trail runs the length of the park for walking, running and biking. It is open from dawn to dusk.

first_step.how: Come to a Walk with Me or Run with Me, using the date and meeting time from the partner events calendar, or fill in the volunteer form to join a cleanup or planting day.
first_step.basis: The walks are free and open to visitors. The site invites new people to bring a friend and lists a volunteer form and a contact form, but it does not say beginners are welcome by name.
first_step.what_to_expect: The walks and runs are free and happen weekly on the park trails. The Friends site does not list meeting points, distances or paces, so check the events calendar first. The site invites new people to bring a friend. For volunteer days, you fill in the online form, and someone from the group contacts you after you submit.
first_visit_tips: Check the events calendar for the walk's meeting point, time and distance before you go.
Take a SEPTA bus to a neighborhood gateway. The park's interactive map shows the closest one, and buses 18 and 26 stop at some gateways.
Watch your footing on the narrow, curved trail. In an emergency, call 911 and give the nearest gateway or intersection.
Send questions through the Contact Us form on the Friends site.

records.notes: Walk days and times are still not confirmed. The partner calendar at ttfwatershed.org/events/ returned HTTP 403 and was not retried, so the record names no days. The Friends site invites new people to bring a friend. Status and last sign of life are carried from tier 1 (the ArcGIS friends group record); the group's own pages show no dated event.

records.name: Tacony LAB Community Art Center
records.summary: A community art center in Tacony that is a program of Mural Arts Philadelphia, run in partnership with the local city council office. It offers free art classes, an open studio, and a Saturday kids club.
records.what_you_do: Take a free painting, drawing, sewing, weaving or laser cutter class, or use the open studio.

schedule.text: The open studio runs more than 30 hours a week. Posted hours: Monday noon to 8 pm, Tuesday 10 am to 8 pm, Wednesday 4 to 8 pm, Thursday noon to 4 pm, and Friday 10 am to 2 pm (closes at noon on First Fridays). Saturdays are open only during kids classes, and the center is closed Sunday.

cost.text: Art classes are free. Many events need advance registration, and most event listings do not show a price. The open studio fee is not stated.

access.notes: The site says the center is wheelchair accessible. It does not mention elevators, parking or transit.

first_step.how: Walk into the open studio during posted hours, or sign up for a free class or event through the events page, which uses Eventbrite.
first_step.basis: Classes are free, the open studio runs posted hours, and the monthly open sew says no experience is needed. Many events need advance registration, so the group is not rated 5.
first_step.what_to_expect: The open studio is for working on a project you bring or starting a new one, alongside the community and staff. Classes are free and cover painting, drawing, sewing, weaving and laser cutter design. The site does not say how long a class runs or how often it meets.
first_visit_tips: Bring a project to work on, or come ready to start something new.
Check the events page first, since many events need an advance sign up.
Call (267) 686-7420 or email info@taconylab.org with questions about classes, parking or transit, since the site does not cover those.

records.notes: The /classes/ page returned HTTP 404, so class length and how often classes meet are not published. The Saturday Kids Club registers through Eventbrite. The visit page confirms the Mural Arts Philadelphia program link and that a city councilmember sponsors the center. The site lists no teen programs, so the tier 1 mention of teen art clubs was removed from the summary.

records.name: Tai Chi in the Square (Franklin Square Tai Chi Group)
records.summary: A free morning tai chi group that practices outdoors at Franklin Square, open to everyone.
records.what_you_do: Practice tai chi outdoors with the group, and move to the pavilion when the weather is cold or wet.

schedule.text: Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays, 7:30 to 8:30 am.

locations.label: Franklin Square, northeast side of the fountain

first_step.how: Go to the northeast side of the fountain at Franklin Square at 7:30 am on a Tuesday, Thursday or Saturday.
first_step.basis: The page says all are welcome at a set place and time, and it describes no sign up. It does not say beginners are welcome by name, and it describes no newcomer program.
first_step.what_to_expect: A free outdoor tai chi session from 7:30 to 8:30 am, with the group gathered at the northeast side of the fountain. The page does not name a leader or describe the class format. On cold, rainy or snowy days, the group moves to the pavilion in the northwest part of the square.
first_visit_tips: Arrive a few minutes before 7:30 am and look for the group by the fountain.
On cold, wet or snowy mornings, look for the group at the pavilion in the northwest part of the square.
Dress for the weather in clothes you can move in.
For updates, the group's Facebook group is the listed way to join.

records.notes: Historic Philadelphia's calendar lists the tai chi session as a weekly event but gives no date or year for it. The October to December Historic District guide PDF could not be read as text, so it was not used. Status is carried from tier 1 because no dated item was found. No WebSearch was spent here.

records.name: Tango Therapy Project
records.summary: A group that teaches adapted Argentine tango to people with Parkinson's, stroke survivors and older adults, and trains volunteers to dance alongside them.
records.what_you_do: Join a weekly tango series of about an hour and a half, with a care partner if you like. Or take the free volunteer training, whose next session is October 18, 2026 at Center in the Park, and help dance with participants during classes.

schedule.text: Adapted tango series meet weekly for 4 to 10 weeks, about 1.5 hours a session. The Center City Parkinson's series meets Wednesday mornings, 10:30 am to 12 pm. The Cherry Hill, NJ series meets Saturday afternoons, 12:30 to 2 pm. Older adult series run on weekday mornings and afternoons in Germantown and Stapeley. Current dates are posted on the site.

locations.label: Center City class site (First Presbyterian Church)
Cherry Hill class site (Katz JCC)
locations.address: 1301 Springdale Rd, Cherry Hill Township, NJ

locations.label: Center in the Park, Germantown (volunteer training and older adult classes)

cost.text: Class fees are not listed on the site. Volunteer training is free.

first_step.how: Email hello@tangotherapyproject.org to ask about joining the Center City series, which started September 16 and runs to November 18, or register for the Cherry Hill series (starts October 10) through its Google Form.
first_step.basis: Classes are open to people with Parkinson's, stroke survivors and older adults, care partners are welcome, and each series has a register link or an email address. The site does not say whether late joining is allowed.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each class lasts about an hour and a half and includes a gentle warm-up, rhythm and balance work, partner practice, some tango steps, dancing, and time for refreshments and talk. Trained instructors lead the class, and volunteers give one-on-one support. The site does not list the class fee.
first_visit_tips: Bring a care partner if you like, since the site welcomes them to class.
Ask about parking, seating and wheelchair access before you go, since the site does not cover them.
Ask whether you can join a series that has already started, because the site does not say and the Center City series began September 16.
The Center City class meets at First Presbyterian Church, 201 S. 21st St.

records.notes: The volunteer page lists tangotherapyproject@gmail.com, but the main site uses hello@tangotherapyproject.org, so the record uses hello@. The summer 2026 post-stroke pilot (Thursdays, July 16 to August 20) has finished, and no next series is listed; ask by email. Intro to Tango presentations are arranged by email for groups and have no set public dates. The Cherry Hill series is in New Jersey.

records.name: Team Keep
records.summary: A nonprofit that helps Philadelphia residents get back the ID papers they need for housing, jobs, benefits, and health care. It holds ID clinics at Free Library branches and works with partner sites.
records.what_you_do: Bring a mailing address to a clinic, where staff help you request birth certificates, photo IDs, and Social Security cards. Staff also run a phone and text line.

schedule.text: Clinics run at Free Library of Philadelphia branches. The Parkway Central clinic meets on the first and third Thursday of each month, 12 to 4 pm, and the clinic calendar on keep.id lists other branch dates.

cost.text: The site does not state a fee for clinic help. It asks for donations.

access.notes: The site says its help is available at accessible places, but gives no specifics.

first_step.how: Call the hotline at 1-844-KEEPID to confirm the next clinic date, and bring a mailing address.
first_step.basis: The clinics are open to the public, and the site gives a phone line and a clinic calendar. It does not say whether you can walk in or need an appointment.
first_step.what_to_expect: At a clinic, staff help you request a birth certificate, photo ID, or Social Security card, and you bring a mailing address. The site does not say how long a visit takes or whether you need an appointment. It asks for donations and does not state a fee.
first_visit_tips: Call 1-844-KEEPID before you go to confirm the clinic date and what papers to bring.
Bring a mailing address, since the site lists one as a clinic requirement.
If you have no ID or no address, ask the hotline first, since the site says help is still available for people with missing IDs or no address.

records.notes: Tier 1 said weekly clinics at six Free Library branches. The group's outreach page instead names the Parkway Central clinic (first and third Thursday, 12 to 4 pm) and lists other partner sites without days. The six-branch claim could not be confirmed, so the schedule uses the outreach page. The clinic calendar on keep.id did not load as text. Free Library calendar listings for Keep ID sessions were found by search, but those pages returned HTTP 403, so none of their dates are used. The outreach page names no eligibility rules, so open_to stays public.

notes: Seven groups researched, all seven records are publish. Budget: 1 of 1 WebSearch used, 23 WebFetch calls used (cap 60). Not blocked but missing: taconylab.org/classes/ returned 404; the keep.id outreach page on the non-team subdomain returned blank text; the Historic Philadelphia guide PDF was not readable as text. No rate limiting was seen beyond the 403 responses. Main changes from tier 1: Tabor's pantry hours (Thursdays 10 am to noon) were found on the pantry page; Tabernacle's newcomer rating dropped from 4 to 3 and its welcome video claim was removed because no link could be found; Tacony LAB's teen art club wording was removed because the site lists only a Saturday kids club; Team Keep's schedule now uses the outreach page's Parkway Central dates, which conflicts with tier 1's six-branch weekly claim; Tango Therapy Project got the current Center City series dates, the October 18, 2026 volunteer training, and the summer 2026 post-stroke pilot status. Tacony Creek walk days are still unconfirmed because the partner calendar is blocked.
